One night the shell whispered of a great storm that would come not from wind, but from forgetting. If people forgot the names of their neighbors, the river would dry and the hills would lose their color. Orla set forth with only the shell’s murmur guiding her, trading stories for stories with every traveler and listening for the quiet between words.

When dawn returned, the village woke to remember—neighbors as a chorus, doors as welcome mouths, light as a shared feast. The storm abated, and the shell slept once more in Orla’s palm.
